Bristol Myers Squibb is combining all research and development efforts under one leader as pressure rises to replenish its pipeline.
Bristol Myers Squibb is reorganizing its R&D unit, with the pharma’s Chief Research Officer Robert Plenge set to leave his role by the end of the year.
The efforts are designed to combine the company’s scientific and clinical expertise to accelerate pipeline development, according to a Thursday release . Previously, the company conducted early research and discovery separately from drug development.
At the start of next year, BMS Chief Medical Officer and development head Cristian Massacesi will lead the “unified” R&D organization, according to the New Jersey pharma. Meanwhile, Plenge—who has been with BMS for over seven years and was at Celgene before the $74 billion acquisition of that company in 2019 —will serve in an advisory capacity through March 2027.
“By combining the strengths of its teams, BMS aims to advance its pipeline with greater speed, sharper focus and a shared commitment to delivering for patients,” the company said in the release.
BioSpace has reached out to BMS for more details about the reorganization, including the potential for layoffs, pipeline changes and the role of AI in its efforts.
BMS has faced scrutiny for its pipeline efforts as the loss of exclusivity for blockbusters Opdivo and Eliquis looms. In 2025, Pfizer-partnered blood thinner Eliquis brought in $14.4 billion in global sales, while PD-1 checkpoint inhibitor Opdivo secured $10 billion worldwide—together accounting for roughly half of BMS’ entire $48.2 billion revenue.
Last month, analysts at BMO Capital Markets were underwhelmed with the company’s plans to prepare for the patent losses, with the key potential revenue replacements in BMS’ pipeline—Cobenfy, milvexian and admilparant—all holding a good amount of risk.
“Bringing research and development together as one organization is an important step in our work to position BMS for long-term growth,” BMS CEO Christopher Boerner said in a prepared statement on Thursday. “This combined R&D organization sets us up to attract and retain the best talent, build critical capabilities, and better integrate new technology.”

Honda has been steadily expanding its electric motorcycle lineup , but one of its most interesting new models isn’t a flashy high-performance machine. It’s a modest little electric scooter called the Honda UC3, and with prices now dipping close to $2,000 in local markets, it’s the kind of affordable electric two-wheeler that many Americans would probably love to get their hands on.
Unfortunately, that’s probably not happening anytime soon.
We first covered the Honda UC3 earlier this year when the company announced plans to launch the electric scooter in Thailand and Vietnam. Designed as an electric equivalent to a 110cc gasoline-powered scooter, the UC3 is built for practical everyday transportation rather than weekend joyrides.
But don’t let its modest appearance fool you. The UC3 packs a 6 kW (8 hp) electric motor capable of reaching approximately 50 mph (80 km/h), making it more than capable of handling typical urban commuting.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Its 3.2 kWh lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery provides up to 76 miles (122 km) of range under WMTC testing. Unlike Honda’s other electric scooters that use removable batteries, the UC3 has a permanently installed battery that charges directly on the bike.
There’s also a full-color TFT display, smartphone connectivity, three riding modes, reverse gear, and a generous 26-liter under-seat storage compartment.
And perhaps most importantly, it comes from Honda, a company with decades of experience building reliable, affordable motorcycles.
So why can’t Americans have nice things?
The UC3 originally launched in Vietnam with prices starting around 78.5 million Vietnamese dong, or roughly $3,000. However, recent reports from Vietnamese dealerships show incentives bringing prices down to around 54 million dong, equivalent to approximately $2,100.
That’s a pretty compelling price for a 50 mph (80 km/h) electric scooter from one of the world’s largest motorcycle manufacturers.
But despite its appeal, Honda hasn’t announced any plans to bring the UC3 to the United States.
And frankly, I wouldn’t hold my breath.
In much of Southeast Asia, scooters are everyday transportation , with millions of riders using them for commuting, shopping, and practically everything else. In the US, motorcycles are much more commonly recreational vehicles, and the market for small, practical scooters is comparatively tiny.
Add in the costs of US regulatory certification, establishing parts and service support, and navigating a market where many buyers expect motorcycles to handle highway speeds, and the business case becomes considerably less attractive.
That’s unfortunate, because the UC3 looks like exactly the kind of electric two-wheeler that could make a real difference in American cities.
It’s affordable, practical, fast enough for most city streets, and backed by a manufacturer that isn’t going anywhere.
Now if only Honda would give Americans a chance to buy one.

Photo: Wan Hai Lines
By Alison Koo
12 November 2026
Wan Hai Lines is ordering more than 110,000 new containers, at a cost of around $325m, as the Taiwanese liner operator expects delivery of 11 new ships next year.
The company disclosed the order yesterday, after unveiling a net profit of $1.29bn for the first nine months of 2026, nearly double that reported a year ago.
The new containers will support the additional capacity and replace older equipment. Some 45,800 boxes, costing $144m, will come from China International Marine Containers (CIMC), 24,200 Pan Ocean Container Supplies ($69.2m), 23,050 from Dong Fang International ($65m), and 17,000 from Singamas ($47.28m).
Wan Hai will take delivery of 11 vessels in 2027, comprising 10 of 16,000 teu and one of 8,700 teu. The larger ships are expected to be deployed on Asia-South America routes, the 8,700 teu vessel could go to Asia-Mediterranean or Asia-Middle East services.
The carrier, which runs standalone transpacific, Asia-Mediterranean, and Asia-South America services alongside its core intra-Asia routes, has already introduced six energy-efficient new ships this year, reducing its fleet’s average age to 8.8 years.
By 2030, Wan Hai expects to receive another 42 vessels, adding around 475,000 teu, as it moves towards a fleet capacity target of 1m teu, placing it in a position to overtake compatriot Yang Ming in the ranks of the top ten carriers.
This quarter, Wan Hai expects intra-Asia routes to benefit from the traditional peak season, supported by holiday stockpiling and inventory replenishment ahead of the lunar new year holiday in February. Freight rates and cargo volumes are expected to increase.
By contrast, deepsea routes are entering their seasonal off-peak period, with transpacific freight rates normalising from Q3 peak levels.
To expand its regional network, Wan Hai plans to launch the CI8 direct service this month, connecting Haiphong, South China, and Malaysia with the West Indies. It will also strengthen services along the west coast of North America, the eastern Mediterranean, and the west coast of South America.
Meanwhile, berths 79 to 81 at Kaohsiung Port’s Fifth Container Terminal became fully operational this month, further expanding Wan Hai’s terminal operating capacity.

Photo: Nissan
Actually, the Nissan Qashqai Heritage Collection isn't a new special edition or even some accessories or apparel collection - it's just a digital archive that chronicles the model's design and innovation history.
Nissan is making some interesting connections these days. For example, in America, the Japanese automaker has decided to mark the special occasion of Nissan Patrol's 75th anniversary in the United States, too, by launching the 2027 Nissan Armada Patrol PRO-4X trim level complete with a few novelties.
Moving to Europe , Nissan Qashqai celebrates 20 years since its 2006 debut at the 2006 Paris Motor Show in France, with the brand often credited with “the creation of the compact crossover blueprint” following its introduction. It’s always been an Old Continent-focused product, with more than 4.1 million units delivered to Europe, but the Qashqai has also registered about half a million sales for global markets during its two-decade tenure.
Today, the Nissan Qashqai is sold in more than 100 countries and has received over 110 international accolades, and the latest version - Qashqai with Nissan e‑POWER hybrid technology – has already reached 250k European customers. Naturally, the brand wanted to mark the occasion of its 20th anniversary and created a bespoke 'Y2K' livery and the Qashqai Heritage Collection.
Back in the early 2000s, buyers of conventional European family cars usually chose between a hatchback, a sedan, a station wagon, a minivan or a true SUV . Nissan's European teams wanted to be different and, instead of bringing a new Almera hatchback to life, went with “a new style of vehicle that combined the best attributes of several categories: the compact footprint, practicality, affordability, simplicity and efficiency of a family hatchback with the robust styling and raised seating position of an SUV.”
The Nissan Qashqai became an instant success with 100k units delivered in just nine months, and Nissan sold one million units by January 2011. Today, the model has reached its third generation since 2021 and was refreshed in 2024, with the e-Power hybrid launched in late 2022 with 157 combined hp and a combined fuel economy of up to 4.3 L/100 km (54.7 mpg), with a maximum range of 1,279 km (795 miles) from a full tank (WLTP), and sprinting to 100 kph or 62 mph in 7.6 seconds.
To mark the occasion of the anniversary, a digital artist and creator called Dale (Heymoonly) Lendl created a unique 'sticker bomb' design with Nissan. The Y2K-style livery “reinterprets early-2000s visual culture through a contemporary lens, using the vibrant neon palette and digital-art influences to celebrate Qashqai's disruptive origins.”
The car was also customized inside and has “fun accessories” like velour seat covers, a colorful steering wheel cover, pop CDs from the era, and even “a functional iPod complete with a mid-2000s playlist.” Cool, right?

By Alex Lennane
12 November 2026
LATAM Cargo is making its largest investment outside freighter aircraft, as airlines and airports turn to technology to tackle missed shipments, recover disrupted flights, and make better use of capacity.
The carrier’s transformation programme, alongside operational tools at Atlas Air and automation projects at Singapore Changi Airport, shows where digital investment is being directed: toward the decisions and processes that determine whether freight moves as promised.
Speaking to The Loadstar at TIACA’s Air Cargo Forum in Miami last month, LATAM Cargo CEO Andrés Bianchi said the programme involved around 18 teams and had already delivered 45 digital products, with five more planned for Q4.
“This is the largest investment LATAM Cargo has ever made in something other than a freighter,” he said, declining to disclose the amount.
The starting point was changing how the company worked, he explained, moving away from traditional departmental silos and identifying where performance needed to improve.
“It’s thinking in a different way in terms of how people work, and then asking them what they need to deliver using technology,” said Mr Bianchi.
LATAM first considers whether existing software can meet its requirements, but he estimated that 80% to 90% of what it needed was worth developing in-house.
For customers, the priorities were reliability, speed and peace of mind. That meant addressing failures such as cargo missing a flight because of a document or communication problem, rather than simply replicating the information services airlines had traditionally offered.
Tracking was another example: customers might want shipment information delivered through a different channel, rather than having to retrieve it from a website.
Better aircraft loading and planning also offered a way to release capacity. Mr Bianchi cited finding an additional 5% payload as an example of the potential benefit on constrained lanes, rather than a quantified result already achieved.
At Atlas Air, chief strategy and transformation officer Martin Drew described a Network Decision Support Tool designed to help untangle disrupted aircraft and crew schedules.
A weather delay, for example, could leave a crew unable to operate its next flight within their permitted hours. Replacing that crew creates further questions about positioning, cost, and whether an aircraft will still reach its maintenance location with enough time and staff available.
Atlas’s operation is particularly complex, because it does not follow a conventional hub-and-spoke pattern, he explained.
The tool produces recommendations within milliseconds, assessing the cost and operational consequences of recovery options, Mr Drew said.
“It’s such a complex sort of jigsaw,” he added. Previously, the exercise had been largely manual and could result in less-effective decisions.
Atlas developed the tools through a transformation team combining internal operational expertise with people recruited from consultants and other airlines. It has also brought data together through a Databricks platform to support decision-making.
Future development includes maintenance planning, aircraft routing, and integrated scheduling of aircraft and crews. Mr Drew also identified opportunities to improve forecasting by examining larger volumes of data.
At Changi Airport, one measurable result comes from coordinating trucks with cargo readiness and warehouse resources.
VP of its cargo business division Jaisey Yip said early results from truck-dock slot booking showed waiting times for cargo lodgement had fallen by about 25%.
Introduced in 2024 for cargo lodgement – submitting documentation electronically to authorities or handlers before the physical cargo arrives – and extended to collection the following year, the system replaces uncoordinated arrivals with planned visits, aligned with shipment readiness and handlers’ available dock capacity.
The airport is working with SATS, dnata, and tech partners. An enhanced version, planned for 2027, would deepen integration with handlers’ cargo management systems and allow multiple slots to be consolidated into one trip.
Changi is also trialling Aircraft 360, using computer vision and AI to monitor milestones during aircraft turnarounds. When a process falls behind, the system alerts operational partners so they can redeploy resources before delays spread.
Ms Yip reported early improvements in turnaround punctuality, but did not quantify them.
Autonomous cargo transport remains another area of testing.
SATS is trialling vehicles to move shipments between its import terminal and forwarders’ warehouses within the airport free trade zone. Driverless baggage tractors are already operating, but extending the technology to cargo towing involves further work.
For LATAM, technology investment also depends on maintaining the people who understand customers’ problems, and can act on the information.
“AI will help you make better decisions,” Mr Bianchi said. “The people at the front are going to make those decisions.”

source_document.body:
Returns are a big and costly ordeal. While a majority of retail focus on getting items to store shelves or doorsteps, what happens afterwards is increasingly becoming a top of mind issue for supply chain executives.
To put things in context, consumers were expected to return $849.9 billion in merchandise in 2025, according to the National Retail Federation. The projection, from NRF and Happy Returns’ 2025 Retail Returns Landscape , equals 15.8% of retail sales, down from $890 billion, or 16.9%, in 2024.
ITF Group, a third-party logistics provider based in Hazelwood, Missouri, argues retailers book part of that cost in the wrong department. Its Retail Reality Check Report , released Sept. 30, traces many returns to how a retailer vets and manages its carriers.
The report lands as retailers pay more to move holiday freight. Contract truckload rates reached a 52-week high of $2.72 a mile plus fuel on Oct. 9, up 18% year over year, according to FreightWaves SONAR data. ITF’s report contends a marginal discount from a lower-cost carrier is often a risk transfer. The cost moves into missed appointment windows that trigger chargebacks, cargo damaged in handling, and returns no one ties back to the freight decision.
“We’ve accepted a false premise in this industry. We talk about returns as if they’re a customer service issue, something e-commerce has to deal with,” Sam Agyemang, ITF’s vice president of business development and sales, said in the report. “In reality, many of those returns are symptoms of an execution failure. And it’s always upstream.”
How handling turns into returns
Agyemang worked on the shipper side of retail before joining ITF. In an interview with FreightWaves, he said returns often get blamed on something that went wrong along the logistics route.
“If you kind of scratch right beneath the surface, supply chain is where everything becomes visible,” he said. “It’s not necessarily where the problems originated from.”
He described a hypothetical hit holiday toy: loaded at its manufacturing origin, palletized for domestic or international shipment, opened and put on a shelf, then boxed again for delivery.
“There are lots of hands that touch these goods along the way,” Agyemang said. “If you aren’t necessarily privy to the process or the relationships that you have throughout the supply chain … you could be sending out product that’s maybe slightly damaged, looks used, etc. And that can be part of your return as well.”
Many shoppers expect the trip back to cost them nothing. In a Kenco survey of more than 350 North American consumers , 47% said they expect free returns.
Agyemang said the retailer then covers the reverse logistics and the work of getting the item back into inventory.
“What procurement is seeing as a good rate for their P&L,” he said, “could now be a customer service issue when they realize that this product was mishandled in the transportation of it.”
Freight costs split across departments
Retailers handle returns, freight cost, and margin timing as three conversations in three departments, the report argues. A product mishandled in a warehouse, it says, surfaces weeks later as a percentage in another department’s report.
“We’re organized, especially in the West, for very segmented structures and departments. They’re not necessarily always talking about their P&L amongst each other,” Agyemang said.
But the public data does not show how many returns start in freight. NRF found 9% of 2025 returns were fraudulent, and its release does not break out how many of the rest involved goods damaged in transit. ITF’s report gives no figure for the share of returns tied to freight handling.
Scoring carriers on more than on-time delivery
The standard carrier scorecard stops when the freight is delivered, according to the report.
“A question every shipper should ask themselves is how many companies measure transportation success only by on-time delivery, and never measure how transportation affects return rates,” ITF CEO Sam Burkhan said in the report.
The report closes with five questions for retailers: whether they track freight’s effect on return rates, score carrier bids on total risk, know where liability sits, vet carriers after onboarding, and build freight relationships before peak.
The liability question has sharpened this year. In May, the U.S. Supreme Court ruled 9-0 in Montgomery v. Caribe Transport II that freight brokers can face state negligent-hiring suits over the carriers they select. The ruling covered brokers. The court did not decide whether shippers carry the same exposure.
“Because of that Montgomery ruling, everyone needs to start rethinking and retraining how they vet their carriers,” Agyemang said. “And unfortunately during your peak season, that’s not when you want to start vetting carriers. You probably can’t rebuild your network in a few weeks in peak, right?”
ITF’s self-reported performance figures
ITF says its operating model is built to catch failures before they become returns, chargebacks, or stockouts. It reports a 98% on-time record across more than 100,000 loads a year. ITF says fraud-related incidents and exposure fell about 90% after it added fraud-prevention and turnaround controls, and it puts its in-transit damage rate at about 0.004%. Damage of that kind can come from causes beyond ITF’s handling, such as improper loading or driver error, the report says.
Returns arrive after peak
In NRF’s 2025 survey, retailers expected 17% of holiday sales to come back, in line with previous years.
“If you’re able to have good vetted carrier relationships from the start, I do feel that you’re going to eliminate a lot of the risk that you will see that will show up in different departments in January,” Agyemang said.
Why it matters: Retailers are paying the highest contract truckload rates in a year to stock shelves for the holidays. If ITF is right, picking the cheapest carrier to offset that cost can create damage and returns that land in January, in budgets procurement never sees.

Chances are you may not five a flying hoot about Cupra’s cars , because the company does not sell any of them in the United States of America. However, if you value your petrolhead license and/or you live in the Old Continent, then you should care about its models, because quite a few of them are on the sporty side of things.
But is the Terramar included? Well, before answering this question, we have to remind you that it comes to life at the Gyor factory in Hungary, where assembly started a little over two years ago, in September 2024. The model has available all-wheel drive, and shares its nuts and bolts not only with its sibling, the Formentor, but also the Audi A3, Q3, Q6, Skoda’s Octavia, Superb, Kodiaq, Volkswagen’s Golf Mk8, Passat, Tiguan, Tayron, T-Roc, Atlas/Teramont, and others.
All of them are based on the Volkswagen Group’s MQB Evo construction, so they are very versatile. In fact, they are so versatile that Cupra’s Formentor is available in the VZ5 configuration . And you know what this means, don’t you? That’s right, it features the famous 2.5-liter five-cylinder turbocharged engine from Audi Sport. So far, this is the only Cupra available with this powertrain, but that’s about to change soon, by the looks of it, because it seems that the Terramar might also go down this route.
Truth be told, we have suspected it from earlier this year, which is when we got the chance to see a sportier looking Cupra Terramar as it was attacking the Nurburgring racetrack in Germany. Our spies believed that it was the Terramar VZ5, and this applies to the tester that recently became the focus of our spy photographer’s camera lens. This one was also caught at the famous racetrack, and it definitely looks a lot more aggressive than the current versions of the crossover.
Photo: Baldauf Mind you, the devil lies in the details, because while the front and rear bumpers are basically the same as before, just like the side skirts and rear diffuser for that matter, this prototype had four round exhaust tips. Just like the Cupra Formentor VZ5 . On top of that, the wheels are bigger, and they appear to be backed up by uprated brakes, which would be a must-have upgrade in order to keep the extra oomph in check. We also expect it to sport some chassis tweaks, likely riding a bit closer to the ground.
But why do the front and rear bumpers look the same as before? Well, chances are these will be replaced with new components that will look a lot sportier once the model is ready to hit the assembly line, and it is probably the Spanish company’s way of hiding the Terramar VZ5 in plain sight. You should also expect the VZ5 logo to decorate the tailgate, and the model to feature some copper accents on the outside, as well as a few upgrades in the cabin.
If it is anything like the Formentor VZ5, then the Cupra Terramar VZ5 should also come with bucket seats featuring extra side bolstering and integrated headrests for the driver and front passenger. The trim and upholstery should be on the exclusive side of things. Some carbon-like trim could be part of the makeover, just like the copper details on the inside, in addition to other things that will further set it apart from the regular Terramar models.
Photo: Baldauf The icing on the cake lies under the hood, and it’s none other than the 2.5-liter five-banger, assuming that this is indeed the VZ5. The mill produces 385 horsepower (390 ps/287 kW) and 354 lb-ft (480 Nm) of torque in the Cupra Formentor VZ5, delivering everything to the AWD system via a 7-speed DSG. From 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 kph), this model takes 4.2 seconds, and that’s 0.3 seconds quicker than Audi’s old RS Q3, which came with the same lump. Flat-out, it will reach 155 mph (250 kph).
But won’t it cannibalize its Formentor sibling? Well, it might just do that, because both the Formentor and the Terramar have an identical wheelbase length of 105.5 inches (2,680 mm). However, the Terramar is a tiny bit larger overall, as it measures 177.9 inches (4,519 mm) in length, 73.3 inches (1,863 mm) in width, and 62.4 inches (1,584 mm) in height. The Formentor is 175.2 inches (4,450 mm) long, 72.4 inches (1,839 mm) wide, and 59.5 inches (1,511 mm) tall. And it is also a bit lighter than the Terramar.
However, while the Formentor is more a coupe crossover, the Terramar is a bit more practical, so they target different clients. And that’s why the Terramar VZ5 won’t cannibalize the Formentor VZ5. Rumor has it that the Cupra Terramar might get the VZ5 treatment sometime in early 2027, as that is when it should officially debut. Are you excited about this new Audi Sport-powered model?

© Nils Prause
By Gavin van Marle
12 November 2026
The recent strength in container spot freight rates drove a 480% year-on-year increase in group profit at Hapag-Lloyd in the third quarter, despite its liner shipping operations seeing flat volumes, indicating lost market share.
Revenue in its liner shipping segment rose 25% year on year in Q3, “driven by a significantly higher average freight rate of $1,808 per teu”, compared with $1,413 per teu in the same period last year.
Its third-quarter volumes reached 3.4m, marginally below last year and clearly below the global market – Container Trades Statistics (CTS) recently released Q3 data showed global volumes growing 5% year on year .
However, Hapag-Lloyd CEO Rolf Habben Jansen said the period had seen exceptionally high levels of vessel utilisation, which had supported the higher freight prices.
“We delivered a strong third quarter, driven by significantly higher spot rates, robust demand and high-capacity utilisation,” he said.
“At the same time, unit costs still remain under pressure due to geopolitical tensions and operational disruptions,” he added.
The carrier appeared to struggle on some of its core lanes – Asia-Europe volumes declined 5.7%, compared with Q3 25, to 927,000 teu, while its transpacific volumes also contracted, by 2.7%, to 1.2m teu.
Vespucci Maritime founder Lars Jensen noted that these declines were broadly similar to those reported by Hapag-Lloyd’s Gemini partner, Maersk, in its third-quarter results, and suggested it was “plausible that capacity restrictions in the Gemini network are part of the reason for volume declines for both Gemini partners”.
In contrast, its carryings to Africa and on other inter-regional trades grew 12.5%, which is much more in keeping with trends noted by CTS. Hapag-Lloyd also reported a 35.1% increase in the average freight rate for these trades.
Meanwhile, the recent completion of its purchase of 25% of the APM Terminals’ Maasvlakte II facility in Rotterdam, as well as the establishment of Brazilian joint-venture to build and operate a new greenfield terminal in Aracruz, saw its port division – Hanseatic Global Terminals (HGT) – inch closer to its target of operating 30 terminals globally by 2030.
HGT officially now has 27 sites in its terminal portfolio, and reported 51% year-on-year growth in Q3 revenue, to $197m, and saw EBIT grow 280%, to $34m.
Container throughput at the terminals in which it has an interest was up 10%, to just under 4m teu.
And the board has raised the outlook for the group this year, with EBITDA now forecast to be between $4.6bn and $5bn, and group EBIT between $2bn and $2.4bn.
“Against the backdrop of volatile freight rates and persistent geopolitical challenges, the outlook is subject to a considerable degree of uncertainty,” the company said.
It also remained confident that its attempt to purchase Israeli carrier Zim, with partner local private equity fund FIMI, would ultimately prove successful, and added that “outstanding approvals are expected to be granted in the first quarter of 2027”.

Peugeot Expands 208 and 2008 Lineups With New Envy Trim Level
7 photos
Photo: Peugeot
Peugeot has decided to make its aging 208 and 2008 lineups a bit more exciting with the introduction of a new trim level called Envy.
Announced by the company’s UK branch, the grade is based on the Allure specification, and as you can assume, it brings a few upgrades both inside and out.
For instance, aluminum door sills that feature the company’s lettering, and glossy black daytime running light surrounds are some of the novelties. On top of these, the 208 hatchback now comes with 16-inch diamond-cut wheels with a Black Mist Varnish. The Noma alloys are joined by glossy black highlights on the front and rear bumpers, and a Black Diamond roof said to be unique to this model.
As for the Peugeot 2008 crossover, it now comes with a set of 17-inch diamond-cut wheels with a Black Mist varnish. The alloys are called Karakoy, the press release reveals. Both models are also available in new exterior colors that are offered as standard. These include the Alvao Green on the supermini and the Nazaro Blue on the subcompact crossover, with the Lion brand stating that other paint finishes are also available for the two.
Usually found from the GT grade upward, the Dynamic front seats can be seen on the inside, wrapped in Tremezzo embossed fabric, which is said to be new. The Opalite stitching is also on deck, and the Peugeot shield is printed on the headrests at the front. The Opalite decorative stitching and co-ordinated inserts can be found on the enhanced door cards, and the Mistral Black roof lining is also a thing on the new Envy trim level.
Photo: Peugeot The equipment list has also been boosted, with the Envy versions of the Peugeot 208 and 2008 being offered with a 180-degree color reversing camera, and keyless entry and go. Moreover, the crossover is also offered with a two-position trunk floor. These add up to the gear found on the Allure grade, which includes stuff such as the head-up digital gauge cluster, and the Peugeot i-Cockpit, as well as the tinted rear windows, and parking sensors at both ends.
Pricing for the 2026 Peugeot 208 Envy starts at 23,115 pounds (equal to $30,760) on-the-road for the Turbo 100 six-speed manual powertrain. The trim level is also available with the Hybrid 110 e-DSC6 assembly, priced from 24,915 ($33,155), as well as the Electric 50 kWh 136 zero-emission powertrain, with pricing starting at 25,565 pounds ($34,020), or 24,065 pounds ($32,025) after the ECG (Electric Car Grant).
As for the 2026 Peugeot 2008 Envy, it can be ordered from 26,165 pounds ($34,820) for the Turbo 100 six-speed manual, and 29,215 pounds ($38,880) for the Hybrid 145 e-DSC6. Moreover, it is also available with the 1.2-liter PureTech 136 eight-speed automatic assembly, with an on-the-road starting price of 28,465 pounds ($37,880), and in the Electric 54 kWh 156 configuration, priced from 29,965 pounds ($39,880), or 28,465 pounds ($37,880) after the ECG.
It is worth noting that since the new Envy grade version of the Peugeot 208 builds on the Allure, it obvious slots between this variant and the superior GT, whereas the Style is found at the bottom end of the lineup, and the GT Premium tops the family. The Peugeot 2008 lineup includes the Allure, Envy, GT, and GT Premium in the United Kingdom, the company’s official local website reveals.
Photo: Peugeot
The E-208, aka the electric version of the supermini, is available in the Allure, Envy, GT, and GT Premium configurations, as well as the new E-208 GTi , with its 277 hp (281 ps/207 kW) and 254 lb-ft (345 Nm) of torque available on tap, which enables 0-62 mph (0-100 kph) in 5.5 seconds. This model has a WLTP range of 233 miles (375 km) with the battery fully charged. As for the E-2008, it is available in the Allure, Envy, GT, and GT Premium trim levels in the UK.
Peugeot’s portfolio also includes the 308 SW, 3008, 408,, 5008, Rifter, and Traveler in the United Kingdom, and depending on the model, they can be ordered either with gasoline, hybrid, of fully electric firepower.
As a reminder, the second-generation Peugeot 208 has been around since 2019, and that is also when its crossover sibling was introduced. Both models are based on the CMP platform, and other vehicles sharing the same underpinnings are the Jeep Avenger, the Opel / Vauxhall Corsa F and Mokka B, the Fiat 600, DS 3 Crossback, Citroen C4 and C4 X, Lancia Ypsilon, and Alfa Romeo Junior, among others. The Dongfeng Aeolus Yixuan and Yixuan GS are also based on this construction.
The Peugeot 2008 was facelifted in May 2023, and its hatchback sibling followed in its footsteps two months later, in July. The updates include the usual revisions on the outside, some tweaks in the cabin, and a few other novelties meant to keep the two models on the appealing side of their classes for a few more years.

2023 Dodge Durango SRT Hellcat Fails To Sell Despite Just 252 Miles on the Clock
26 photos
Photo: Bring a Trailer
The market for used Hellcat-spec Durango SUVs is a bit wobbly right now. It's hard to get a sense of where you're at, especially if you're trying to sell a low-mileage example. For instance, we've seen both sub-$70k and $80k+ valuations this year, depending on mileage, and one particular model that seems pretty much identical to this one, sold for $67,500 back in May.
To be fair, that was a 2021 model year vehicle, and this one is 2023MY - acquired new for $133,835 by the same person who tried to get rid of it at auction these past few days. Sadly, the reserve wasn't met, which comes as a surprise if I'm being honest. The top bid stood at $72,500 and clearly that wasn't enough. Why? I have no idea. There's no way this is an $80,000 SUV right now.
Maybe the seller was hoping for $75,000, but even that feels like a bit of a stretch. And yes, I did factor in the mileage (252 miles). I still wouldn't have held out for $75,000. Not just because it's a "hard sell", pun intended. But also because on top of the $72,500 bid, you need to factor in the buyer's fee, shipping and whatnot.
There's also an issue with high-performance SUVs in general when it comes to long-term collectibility and value retention. There's a massive difference between a vehicle that impresses you today, when it's new or just a few years old, and one that people dream of owning 15-20 years from now. I'm not sure any modern-day SUV, regardless of brand and performance, will be as desirable in the future as it is today.
People collect classic Mustangs and Chargers, not Willys Jeeps and C/K Chevys. I mean, they collect those too, but they don't spend fortunes on them, and they certainly don't dream about one day owning one.
Anyway, specs-wise, this Durango comes with Gunmetal over-the-top stripes spread across the Destroyer Gray (PDN) colorway, to go with a sunroof, bi-function LED headlights, a vented hood, roof spoiler, power-operated liftgate, plus a set of Lights-Out 20" alloy wheels rocking Pirelli P Zero rubber and red-finished calipers. The vehicle also comes with adaptive damping suspension, four-wheel traction control, Ready Alert Braking (RAD), and Trailer Sway Control.
Photo: Bring a Trailer Meanwhile, interior highlights include the heated and ventilated front seats, heated second-row bucket seats, folding third-row seats, silver accent stitching throughout the cabin, a ParkView rearview camera, three-zone automatic climate control, adaptive cruise control, a Harman Kardon sound system, and a leather-wrapped steering wheel with paddle shifters.
As for the engine, it's a supercharged 6.2-liter HEMI V8 , good for 710 horsepower and 645 lb-ft of torque. Everything gets sent to all four wheels via a TorqueFlite eight-speed automatic gearbox.
The Durango SRT Hellcat is capable of hitting 60 mph (97 kph) in about 3.5 seconds, before covering a quarter mile in just under 12 seconds. Technically, this is an 11-second SUV.

The 2027 Hopper 5 WL Is a Little Tin Box That Lacks for Nothing
15 photos
Photo: Modern Buggy RV
There is truth to that saying about strong essences being kept in small bottles, and the new travel trailer slash squaredrop from Modern Buggy RV wants to prove it to you. It's called the Hopper 5 WL and it's a stick-and-tin towable that hopes to check all the boxes you need.
Or, as Michigan-based manufacturer Modern Buggy, or ModBug for short, likes to say, "we don't want you to need anything more" than what you get with the Hopper 5 WL.
Introduced at the end of September 2026 as a 2027 unit, this is just one of the new addition to the Hopper series of lightweight and affordable towables from Modern Buggy. It's also part of the WL sub-series, where "WL" stands for "Woodline," a reference to the fact that this doesn't come with the all-fiberglass construction of the non-WL models.
Instead, it's a traditional stick-and-tin construction, and Modern Buggy is the first to emphasize that. That makes the Hopper 5 WL affordable – definitely more affordable than its fiberglass peers – while maintaining a reduced weight and still offering home-like comforts.
Photo: Modern Buggy RV Despite the number 5 in the name, the 5 WL is actually among the smaller entries in the Hopper series. Modern Buggy boasts that it can be towed even by smaller SUVs, which, together with its ability to sleep a family of four, should increase its appeal.
Long story short, it's a traditional aluminum-sided squaredrop that nonetheless goes the extra mile to cover all the basics and provide as much comfort as its footprint and budget will allow. It's an admirable attempt, and Modern Buggy makes sure they also deliver something extra in terms of looks and some autonomy.
Considering that they also promise proof that "you don't need a massive camper to make big memories," I'd say that these are all things that they must check if they want to be taken seriously. Which they obviously do .
Photo: Modern Buggy RV The Hopper 5 WL comes in at 16.5 feet (5 meters) of length and tips the scales at just 2,700 lbs (1,224 kg). It's designed primarily as a couple's RV, but it can offer accommodation overnight for as many as four people, even all of them adults, thanks to a combination of fixed bed and a convertible dinette.
Construction is with a custom steel chassis with a single axle specced for light offroading. That means a Dexter torsion suspension, beefy offroad tires, and 14 inches (35 cm) of ground clearance.
Being a stick-and-tin trailer means a wooden frame with aluminum sheeting, but Modern Buggy throws in an Azdel-backed single-piece fiberglass roof for good measure, a covered underbelly, and proper insulation to make this an extended seasonal camper.
Photo: Modern Buggy RV Again, they have to do all this, more or less, because they promise a towable with everything inside.
The layout is fairly common in the industry, with a booth dinette with a Lagun table that helps to convert the entire space into a bed, and a fixed east-to-west bed at the back. The galley kitchen is on the campside, to the left of the entrance, and the super compact wet bathroom is located right across from it.
Both these spaces are very cramped, which reduces their everyday functionality. The kitchen, for example, comes with a two-burner gas cooktop under a glass cover and a sink that takes up the remaining counter space, leaving zero space for meal prep.
Photo: Modern Buggy RV You also get storage under the counter and overhead, and a 12V fridge with freezer across the way. It's not much even for a mobile kitchen, and while it won't allow you to throw elaborate dinner parties, it will work just fine for a quick breakfast in two or four.
The bathroom is a cubicle with a plumbed toilet sat on an elevation of the shower tray, but you'd still have to sit down to use the included shower wand. Again, it's not much, but it is a functional, if cramped, bathroom inside a compact travel trailer.
Storage options are a bit more generous and suitable for a party of four. They include large compartments under the dinette benches and under the bed, but also in overhead cabinets throughout, finished in a nice White Latte color.
Photo: Modern Buggy RV Modern Buggy offers standard a 13,500-BTU roof-mounted AC unit, a Fogatti on-demand water heater, and a Suburban propane furnace, thus offering comfort regardless of temperatures outside. A marine-grade deep-cycle battery with disconnect is mentioned on the official page of the trailer, but its capacity isn't.
Also included is a composite entry step, an outside shower, hand-made valances with blackouts on all windows, self-adjusting electric brakes, and 16 gallons (60 liters) for freshwater and 32 gallons (121 liters) each for gray and black water.
The Hopper 5 WL comes prepped for flex solar, a power awning, and a tire carrier with a spare tire.
Photo: Modern Buggy RV Described as "perfect for those who crave adventure" but don't want to break the bank to pursue it or, on the contrary, compromise on personal comfort, the Hopper 5 WL is already out on dealer lots, with selling pricing starting at $20,000, depending on options.
From what I can tell, there are no extended video tours of this new floorplan online yet, so the brief walkthrough at this link will have to do.

At long last! The good folks over at the racing-focused ' Import 2 Race ' channel on YouTube are finally back dwelling around their usual venue, which is Island Dragway in Great Meadows, New Jersey, a track that’s been around since it was established back in 1960!
Well, that was a very long detour! We have been patiently waiting over the course of many weeks for the host of the channel to get back from their lengthy tour focused on roll racing events. They showed us many cool and dramatic encounters in a series of 65-mph roll race battles, with all the high-speed action taking place at the iconic Pocono Raceway , a 2.5-mile tri-oval track in Blakeslee, Pennsylvania.
After that, the videographer changed the scenery but not also the racing format and found a 45-mph roll racing event called the 2026 Sunday Funday Mod2Fame , which took place at an airport in Sullivan County, New York – the format was the 45-mph roll race variety because, obviously, their strip isn’t as long as the massive straight at Pocono. Alas, that didn’t mean the action was any lesser.
Now, at long last, they are back at Island Dragway, and the inaugural skirmish is between two Mopar representatives: a crimson and black-striped L-bodied Dodge Charger sedan, identified as an SRT Hellcat model featuring the 6.2-liter supercharged V8 with more than 700 ponies on tap, while its opponent is a lesser Challenger Scat Pack 1320. The latter comes from the factory with the larger 6.4-liter (392ci) Hemi V8 but makes 485 hp because it’s naturally aspirated.
However, judging by the looks of the crimson Charger and the description offered for the grey and Hemi-striped Challenger, they were both non-standard aftermarket builds, with the Dodge coupe also packing a Whipple supercharger kit, not just dedicated dragstrip tires and alloy wheels like the Charger sedan.
Anyway, the final judgment was done on the track, and both looked ready for a massive skirmish after the pre-race smoke-filled burnouts. The start was a great one for both as they darted like arrows in their lanes and went head-to-head for the duration of the race. Apparently, only one of the track’s electronic scoreboards was functional, but luckily the videographer showed us on the screen the other result, confirmed afterward with the timeslip: only one of the Mopars won the skirmish!
We’re kidding; of course one of the Dodges won the race with a time of 9.78s at no less than 144 mph versus the runner-up’s 10.22s effort at 131 mph. Now, let’s check out the video together to see who’s who. By the way, even though the eighth-generation Dodge Charger has been around for some time and even has a new Super Bee for the 2027 model year, we’re still waiting on a Hemi V8 version…

Delivery management software maker FarEye turned its first quarterly profit in the three months ended March 31, closing a fiscal year in which revenue from Europe, the Middle East and Africa rose 51.17%. The India-based company’s annual net loss narrowed to $1.07 million from $5.90 million.
Since its $100 million fundraising in 2021 , FarEye has continued to expand its global business. Over the past five years, its North America and EMEA businesses together have added more than four times as much new revenue as its APAC business in FY26.
Many of FarEye’s larger customers operate across multiple geographies, so regional revenue attribution doesn’t always reflect the full geographic footprint of these relationships, the company told FreightWaves.
Americas revenue grew 13.25% to $7.97 million in fiscal 2026, while EMEA revenue reached $10.4 million, Nahata said in written responses to FreightWaves. Companywide revenue from operations rose 24.58% to $27.90 million. FarEye reports in Indian rupees and converted every year at 88.37 rupees per dollar, so currency swings do not affect the growth rates.
Nahata said the last mile is the only part of the supply chain that customers actually see.
“Delivery has shifted from being just the final step of an order to a crucial part of what customers expect,” he said. “Unfortunately, a lot of decision-makers still measure success by cost per delivery instead of focusing on customer retention.”
Enterprise customers and competition
FarEye ended the year serving 13 customers that are Fortune Global 500 companies or their group entities, four of them added in fiscal 2026. Customers with annual revenue of $500 million or more produced 70.86% of revenue from operations.
Nahata said Maersk uses FarEye to get more out of its Ground Freight capacity. In the U.S., he pointed to Tractor Supply, which uses FarEye’s AI tools to coordinate its fleet with third-party delivery networks across more than 2,400 stores.
U.S. online demand is still climbing. E-commerce made up 17.1% of U.S. retail sales in the second quarter and grew 12.2% from a year earlier, while total retail sales rose 6.7%, according to the Census Bureau’s second-quarter 2026 Quarterly Retail E-Commerce Sales report .
Competition for large retail accounts has also shifted. Illustrating the example, Ingka Group, Ikea’s largest retailer, bought AI-powered logistics platform Locus in October 2025 and kept it serving its existing enterprise clients.
How FarEye narrowed its loss
Revenue from operations rose $5.51 million in fiscal 2026 while total expenses rose $0.96 million.
“This means that for every extra dollar we earned, our costs increased by only about 17 cents,” Nahata said.
He credited AI tools in operations and product development, saying employee costs stayed almost the same year over year. The company did not say which tasks those tools took over or how its headcount changed.
Subscription gross margin rose to 79.42% from 73.44% in fiscal 2025 and 67.38% in fiscal 2024. Subscription revenue, generated under committed multiyear contracts, made up 83.25% of revenue from operations.
“While AI has played a role in this progress, especially in our operations and product development, I wouldn’t say it’s the only factor,” Nahata said. “The overall improvement comes from a combination of a better product, greater scale, and higher productivity.”
PILOT launched after the fiscal year
FarEye launched PILOT, an agentic AI dispatcher for last-mile hubs , in April, after the fiscal year closed, so the tool is not reflected in these results. It handles scheduling, routing, driver assignment and delivery exceptions, with dispatchers able to approve or override its decisions.
“A dispatch team needs to understand what the system is doing and step in when a situation requires judgment,” Nahata said.
The company has not disclosed how many customers run PILOT in production or quantified its financial impact.
No profit forecast for fiscal 2027
FarEye has not issued a profit forecast for fiscal 2027, and it did not disclose the size of its fourth-quarter profit or revenue.
Cash reserves stood at $30.63 million at year-end, and Nahata said FarEye can now serve more customers without costs rising at the same pace.
“While we’re not ready to give profit projections for FY27 yet, I believe FY26 was a crucial step in showing that kind of growth,” Nahata said.
Why it matters: U.S. retailers signing multiyear delivery software contracts are betting on a vendor’s staying power. FarEye now has a profitable quarter behind it and a growing list of clients

By Charlotte Goldstone
12 November 2026
The coming influx of larger containerships could render ageing panamax vessels commercially obsolete by 2030, while carriers’ efforts to renew smaller fleets threaten further capacity displacement.
Jonathan Roach, analyst at Braemar, told The Loadstar the newbuilding programme was creating a substantial mismatch between vessels entering service and those approaching retirement.
He identified the 4,000–7,499 teu segment as particularly vulnerable, with 428 vessels aged at least 20 years old against just 283 ships on order.
As larger newbuildings enter service, existing vessels could be cascaded into trades traditionally served by smaller ships, intensifying competition for employment.
Mr Roach said: “The ageing fleet is concentrated in the sub-panamax segment, while the orderbook is heavily skewed towards larger ships.”
He warned that traditional panamax and post-panamax vessels could become increasingly squeezed, “potentially becoming obsolete by 2030”.
However, new analysis from Alphaliner suggests fleet renewal will also reshape the smaller vessel segments.
Mael Pape-Leostic, shipping analyst at Alphaliner, told The Loadstar the orderbook remained heavily weighted towards large containerships destined for mainline services.
But he noted a significant increase in orders for vessels of less that 6,000 teu since mid-2025, largely intended to replace ageing tonnage.
Mr Pape-Leostic said: “In our view, this renewal will not be on a like-for-like basis,” and explained that carriers historically deploying vessels below 1,000 teu, could replace them with ships of 1,200 teu or even 1,800 teu.
Alphaliner’s fleet data illustrates the scale of the change. Its figures show 526 vessels of less than 1,000 teu are aged at least 20 years old, compared with just 67 ships of that size on order.
Meanwhile, the 1,500–1,999 teu segment has 248 ships on order, compared with 196 vessels aged at least 20 years.
Source: Alphaliner
The figures suggest that the replacment of older vessels with larger ships could increase the global fleet’s carrying capacity without an increase in vessel numbers.
Alphaliner’s data also shows the largest newbuildings dominating capacity additions, with 291 ships of at least 18,000 teu on order, representing 6.06m teu.
Sea-Intelligence forecasts average quarterly deliveries of 1m teu between 2027 and 2030, substantially exceeding recent historical levels.
Mr Roach said: “This is not simply a story of fleet growth. It is a story of fleet displacement… T he influx of larger newbuildings will trigger further cascading, pushing bigger ships into trades currently served by smaller vessels.
“Of course, larger ships cannot serve every trade, so investment in smaller vessels will continue. But the direction of travel is clear – the global fleet is getting bigger, while parts of the existing mid-sized fleet risk being left behind.”
The changing fleet composition could also intensify pressure on charter market earnings. Mr Roach believes charter earnings peaked this year, with 2027 marking the beginning of a downturn.
“Pressure should become more pronounced in 2028, before the market bottoms out in 2029,” he explained.
However, Peter Sand, chief analyst at Xeneta, told The Loadstar that although charter earnings would come under pressure, he did not anticipate a market collapse. He argued that tonnage providers had become more disciplined in recent years, limiting the severity of any downturn.
He also noted that chartered tonnage represented approximately half of carriers’ operational capacity.
Jan Tiedemann, VP of liner strategy at Alphaliner, told The Loadstar longer trade routes, slow-steaming and growing consumption in emerging markets could absorb some additional capacity.
He also pointed to higher bunker and emissions costs, port constraints, and trade imbalances as factors increasing tonnage requirements.

Court Orders JLR To Destroy Seized BYD Files in 24 Hours
8 photos
Photo: BYD
A Dutch court has ordered Jaguar Land Rover to destroy the digital files seized from BYD’s Dutch offices or face a penalty of 50,000 euros per hour. JLR chose the Dutch court because it was counting on the Netherlands’ strict intellectual property laws.
50,000 euros or roughly $55,460. That is how much Jaguar Land Rover has to pay for every single hour of delay until it destroys the digital files seized from BYD. Judge H.F.R. van Heemstra issued the preliminary ruling at the District Court of The Hague, overturning an evidence raid conducted over intellectual property claims involving the BYD Ti7 SUV in August.
The ruling immediately invalidates JLR's earlier seizure and sets strict compliance deadlines. This means that JLR must instruct the court-appointed custodian and bailiff to destroy all seized files within 24 hours. The records had been held by an independent custodian and were never handed directly to JLR.
Failing to issue the destruction order triggers a fine of 50,000 euros per hour, capped at 500,000 euros (approximately $555,000). JLR must also provide BYD with independent confirmation within 24 hours after the data is entirely deleted.
Photo: tthg 04 | TikTok The court banned JLR from taking further steps under the original seizure order, attaching a separate 500,000-euro penalty for each violation. Furthermore, the judge dismissed JLR’s request to fine BYD 500,000 euros for alleged non-compliance with the original raid, finding provisionally that BYD had cooperated. However, BYD was still ordered to pay 25,376.57 euros ($28,110) in legal costs, the Chinese media reports .
Jaguar Land Rover has been there before. Back in 2020, it lost a trial in London, when it tried to trademark the 3D shape of the classic Land Rover Defender 90 and 110 in an attempt to block entrepreneur Sir Jim Ratclie from building the Ineos Grenadier .
JLR appealed the decision to the High Court of England and Wales, where Judge Melissa Clarke dismissed the appeal in August 2020. The Grenadier went into production unbothered in July 2022, and deliveries started later that year, in December.
This time, it all started back in August 2026 when bailiffs acting on behalf of JLR raided BYD's European offices , which are located in Schiedam and Hoofddorp, the Netherlands, secure internal digital records in a surprise move.
Photo: tthg 04 | TikTok BYD labeled the seizure as an overly broad fishing expedition that swept up unrelated proprietary research and development data. JLR reportedly asked for the raid to be fast-tracked so that the suspicious files would be secured before they could potentially be altered or deleted.
JLR accused BYD of dismantling a Land Rover Defender to reverse-engineer its technology and copying its boxy exterior design for the Ti7 SUV , which is sold in China as the Fangcheng Bao Ti7. The model has yet to launch in Europe, with UK deliveries slated for early 2027. The Ti7 undercuts Land Rover Defender in its home market by nearly 20,000 pounds ($26,740).

This Low-Profile Motorhome Is the Smallest of Its Kind but Unbelievably Elegant
18 photos
Photo: Kabe AB
Low-volume RV specialist Kabe AB says they're "always a step ahead," presumably of the competition. The Novum c720 LGB motorhome isn't highlighted as an example of what makes them different from the rest, but it probably should be.
This is the smallest motorhome on offer from Kabe , with the original floorplan introduced a couple of years back under the longer name Novum Compact 720 LGB. For 2027, the model comes with a simplified name and a refreshed interior that brings it, despite the comparatively smaller dimensions, on equal footing with its bigger siblings.
Kabe is a name that probably won't ring many bells for readers outside of Europe. Based in Sweden, it's more of a boutique-style manufacturer of travel trailers and motorhomes, both low profile and fully integrated, that stand out for their sleek, elegant style and quality work.
Kabe products are more expensive than average; they might even be described as pricey among their premium peers, but they're built almost entirely in-house, which ensures excellent quality control. They delivery the quality, the functionality, and the looks, and the same also applies to this compact motorhome.
Photo: Kabe AB The Novum c720 LGB is the smallest of the Novums . It comes in at 7.16 meters (23.5 feet) of total length and 2.24 meters (7.3 feet) of width, and it's offered standard with a maximum permissible weight of 3,500 kg (7,716 lbs), which means you can still operate it on a standard B Category driving license without needing to upgrade.
Like all Novum or, for that matter, Kabe motorhomes, this one sits on a Mercedes-Benz Sprinter chassis, offered standard with a 9-speed automatic transmission and all the extra features that are standard, including a backup camera. The interior, on the other hand, is purely Kabe, with gorgeous cabinetry and elegant finishes.
The layout doesn't do much in terms of breaking the mold of interior compact RV design , but the style elevate it into a class of its own. The shell comes with sandwich construction and Ecoprim insulation in the floor, ceiling, and walls, so this is a motorhome that will remain as comfortable in sub-freezing temperatures as it will be in hot weather.
Photo: Kabe AB Inside, the walls are covered in breathable, soft-touch fabrics of different textures and colors to match each separate space. For instance, in the bedroom, you have an intimate alcove vibe with dark padded walls that match the headboard, while in the dining area, the fabrics are lighter in color and style.
The layout puts a convertible dinette at the front, under a large, curbed skylight, a galley kitchen in the middle of the RV with a wet bathroom across, and the bedroom at the back. To be able to offer a rear pass-through garage that would fit personal luggage as well as adventure gear like a pair of bicycles, Kabe lifts the beds in the bedroom on a platform, creating more headroom underneath.
Then, in the garage, they add metal shelving, netted cubbies, more shelves of wood, and tie-downs on the walls and on the floor. A pass-through garage under an elevated bed is not new, but out of all of them, this is perhaps the neatest, best organized around. And that 's the Kabe difference.
Photo: Kabe AB Upstairs in the bedroom, you have two longitudinal single beds on an aluminum frame that you can join by pulling out an extension and adding inserts into a king bed. You have two more skylights here for ventilation and natural light to offset the darkness of the walls, wraparound cabinetry , prep for a second TV, and beautiful accent lighting.
Additional storage space is built into the base of the beds, in the form of two wardrobes.
At the front, the dinette uses face-to-face benches and the swiveling captain seats to create a space that could accommodate up to five people around the two-fold adjustable table. Overhead cabinets with curved faces and real wood construction, open cubbies in the driver's cab, and prep for a TV on the wall by the door are standard.
Photo: Kabe AB The kitchen is compact, as is customary in Europe – and specced with the basics. A two-burner gas cooktop and a stainless sink under separate glass covers, a Thetford fridge with freezer, an extractor, and lots of drawers and cubbies with central locking are all included.
Unlike in other European motorhomes, the kitchen is as elegant as the rest of the spaces, and because of it, an integral part of them.

Never Registered Chevelle SS 454 LS6 4-Speed Found in Tennessee, It Might Make Purists Frown at It
55 photos
Photo: YouTube/Patrick Glenn Nichols Musclecar Barn Finds
Decades of relentless digital hunting, viral barn-find videos, and nationwide auction mania have driven enthusiasts into believing that virtually every forgotten American muscle car has already been dragged into the sunlight. With millions of eyes scouring satellite maps and rural backroads daily, the odds of unearthing an undocumented Detroit legend seem non-existent. Yet against all logic, dusty garages and quiet country sheds across America still harbor secret big-block treasures waiting to be rediscovered.
That enduring magic recently proved itself again when collector and authenticator Patrick Glenn Nichols acquired a previously unknown 1970 Chevrolet Chevelle SS 454 LS6. Purchased in East Tennessee north of Knoxville in the Bristol Tri-Cities region, this rare hardtop coupe had remained completely off the radar of marque historians since rolling off the Lakewood assembly line in Atlanta, Georgia.
Accompanied by its original factory build sheet, the Chevelle carries a scheduled production date of March 2, 1970, and was delivered new through Bill Conner Chevrolet in Muncie, Indiana. Ordered in solid Code 14 Cortez Silver without hood stripes over a black vinyl bench-seat cabin, the car was configured as a no-nonsense street brawler lacking power steering, a cowl induction hood, or even a radio, retaining its dashboard block-off plate.
Despite skipping creature comforts, the original buyer checked several scarce Regular Production Options on the build sheet, led by RPO NK1, the $34.80 custom cushioned-rim steering wheel. Available across all 1970 Malibu Sport Coupes, Convertibles, and El Caminos, total RPO NK1 production reached just 3,078 units out of 588,022 eligible mid-size cars, making it a genuinely rare feature even for seasoned collectors.
Photo: Facebook/Patrick Glenn Nichols Scanning the build sheet reveals some other rare options installed on this coupe: RPO LS6, the 450-horsepower 454-cubic-inch V8 fitted to only 4,475 Chevelles and El Caminos in 1970; RPO M22, the heavy-duty 4-speed manual transmission installed in 5,410 of 311,553 mid-size Chevys; and RPO Z15, the SS 454 package ordered on 8,773 Malibu coupes, convertibles, and El Caminos, alongside 3,823 Monte Carlos carrying the equivalent Z20 code.
Beyond its powertrain, the build sheet documents other low-volume Chevelle options, including U14 special dashboard gauges (37,378 cars), and the T60 heavy-duty battery at 46,890 orders. Rounding out the paperwork are F41 suspension (56,051 units), G80 Positraction with GY2 3.31:1 gear ratios (64,169 copies), or PL4 F70x14 white-letter tires (64,758 examples).
On the more common side, this muscle car rocks JL2 disc brakes (same as the 139,856 units who came with them), or J50 power brakes, fitted on 180,113 Chevrolets for the 1970 model year.
Photo: YouTube/Patrick Glenn Nichols Musclecar Barn Finds Built before plants switched to dual-snorkel air cleaners in late March 1970, this coupe originally carried an open-element air cleaner and a small radiator. After 56 years, the Chevelle is not an untouched survivor, yet it retains an authentic, date-correct LS6 V8. Cast in February 1970, the 512-code block was decked during a rebuild, erasing its stampings, but wears genuine 291 rectangular-port heads, a factory aluminum manifold, and 3-inch exhaust.
During its restoration, a previous owner installed reproduction quarter panels, bumpers, wheels, interior upholstery, a larger radiator, power steering, a passenger mirror, and a reproduction cowl induction hood with black stripes. The after-market engine bay cover is best identified by an upward front gap, big enough for the authenticator, registrar, YouTuber, and all-around LS6 know-it-all to fit his hand through.
A replacement M22 4-speed with a Hurst linkage and curved Muncie lever sends power to a replacement rear axle. Now certified by Nichols, the coupe will join the 400-odd LS6s in the registry. And if that begs the question “Why is it so important to have them documented somewhere,” I invite you to take a walk down memory lane.
Photo: YouTube/Patrick Glenn Nichols Musclecar Barn Finds Back in 1961, Chevrolet inaugurated the Super Sport badge on the full-size Impala, launching the muscle era with the legendary 409-cubic-inch V8, later joined by other legendary powerhouses from the Chevrolet arsenal. However, during the early days of the “SS” fashion, the Bowtie went liberal, and allowed all engines under the Super Sport umbrella, including Sixes.
As enthusiasts increasingly favored lighter mid-size coupes, Chevrolet retired the Impala SS after 1969, bestowing the Super Sport crown solely onto its intermediates.
Introduced for the 1964 model year to bridge the gap between the compact Chevy II Nova and the full-size Impala, the Chevrolet Chevelle remained in production from 1964 through 1977 across three distinct A-body generations. The performance-oriented Chevrolet Chevelle SS accompanied the lineup from 1964 to 1973, starting as the Malibu SS with 283-cubic-inch and 327-cubic-inch V8s before evolving into the standalone big-block SS 396 series between 1966 and 1968.
Photo: YouTube/Patrick Glenn Nichols Musclecar Barn Finds By 1969, the Super Sport reverted to an option package, setting the stage for the restyled 1970 Chevelle Malibu sport coupe, which carried a base price of $2,809. Selecting the entry-level RPO Z25 SS 396 package added $445.55 and installed a 402-cubic-inch V8 big-block (still badged as a 396; not to be confused with the 400-cuber small-block, also introduced in 1970).
The 402-cube 396 V8 produced 350 horsepower in standard L34 trim or 375 horsepower with the optional $252.80 L78 solid-lifter engine or aluminum-head L89 V8 upgrade.
Buyers ordering a 1970 Chevelle SS could pair those big-block engines with a standard Muncie 3-speed manual on the base 350-horsepower model, a wide-ratio M20 or close-ratio M21 4-speed manual, a heavy-duty M22 4-speed manual, or a 3-speed Turbo Hydra-Matic 400 automatic transmission. When General Motors lifted its “one-cubic-inch per ten pounds of body weight” displacement ban on intermediates for 1970, Chevrolet unleashed the Chevelle SS 454, keeping it until the end of 1973.
Photo: YouTube/Patrick Glenn Nichols Musclecar Barn Finds Stepping up to the 1970 Chevelle SS 454 required selecting RPO Z15 for $503.45, which bundled the 360-horsepower LS5 454-cubic-inch V8, F41 heavy-duty suspension, power front disc brakes, dual exhausts, a blacked-out grille, a domed hood, and 14-inch sport wheels with F70x14 tires.
Checking RPO LS6 cost an extra $263.30, requiring either the $221.80 M22 4-speed or the $290.40 Turbo Hydra-Matic automatic and adding solid lifters, forged internals, and high-flow rectangular-port cylinder heads.
Displacing 454 cubic inches (7,439 CCs) with an 11.25:1 compression ratio, a forged steel crank, forged aluminum pistons, an aluminum manifold, and an 800-cfm Holley four-barrel carburetor, the LS6 delivered 450 horsepower at 5,600 rpm and 500 lb-ft of torque (678 Nm) at 3,600 rpm. Offered in the Chevelle and El Camino for 1970 only across 4,475 total units, the LS6 returned in 1971 solely inside 188 examples of the Corvette (but rated at only 425 horsepower, due to a lowered compression).
Photo: YouTube/Patrick Glenn Nichols Musclecar Barn Finds In 1970 trim, the Chevelle SS 454 LS6 rocketed from 0 to 60 mph in 5.4 seconds, cleared the quarter-mile in 13.1 to 13.7 seconds at 107 mph, and reached 130 mph flat out. Tightening emissions and soaring insurance rates killed the Chevelle LS6 after a single season. Now you see why this Cortez Silver coupe uncovered in East Tennessee is emblematic?
Finally, a word to those who start having wishful thoughts about this day-two renovation: it’s already been sold, so the point of asking about a price is no more.

Xiaomi Appears To Have Run Out of Steam, Despite Promising SkyNomad Sales in October
89 photos
Photo: Xiaomi
Xiaomi prepares to end 2026 with a mixed bag of achievements and is likely to miss its self-imposed sales target despite encouraging SkyNomad sales. This showcases the challenges of staying ahead in the tough Chinese market, where new models have a shelf life of less than a year. Despite a recent refresh, the SU7 sales have stalled, and the YU7 has been dragging its feet for a while, so SkyNomad's success might not last long.
Xiaomi's story is one of the most impressive in the automotive industry. The technology company, known just a few years ago for its phones and IoT devices, established itself as a carmaker and rose to the top of car sales in China. This is no small feat, especially considering the highly competitive Chinese market. The mighty Apple tried to make a car before Xiaomi, and broke its teeth after burning over $10 billion.
Every single model Xiaomi launched has been a bestseller in its segment, at least for a period. The SU7 quickly moved past the Tesla Model 3 in the sales charts, and it looked unstoppable. The YU7 had some good months surpassing the Tesla Model Y, although that didn't last long. As soon as Xiaomi released the refreshed SU7 early this year, the YU7's sales stalled. At the same time, orders for the electric sedan spiked.
Xiaomi's SkyNomad brand reported encouraging sales in October The same story repeated with Xiaomi's new car brand SkyNomad. Launched with great fanfare on September 7 in China, SkyNomad quickly became the public's favorite. The brand focuses on range-extended SUVs, unlike Xiaomi's core models SU7 and YU7, which are exclusively offered as battery-electric vehicles.
The first SkyNomad models, the N70 and N90, accounted for over 54% of Xiaomi's sales in October, the first full calendar month on sale since launch. The former sold 14,558 units, while the larger and more expensive N90 contributed 12,589 units to the tally. Xiaomi previously reported over 70,000 firm orders for the SkyNomad vehicles.
Photo: Xiaomi Auto SkyNomad's numbers look even more impressive considering the overall market slump in October. Passenger vehicle sales fell 27% in October, while the new energy segment (which combines BEVs, EREVs, and PHEVs) dropped 13.7%. This marks the tenth consecutive month of decline, helping SkyNomad's results shine even brighter.
Xiaomi's core EV models have already become obsolete Xiaomi reported total sales of 50,168 vehicles in October, a 25.4% gain from September. However, sales of the SU7 sedan, which was recently refreshed, fell 17.6% to 12,984 units, while the YU7 dropped 15.1% to 10,037. This shows that SkyNomad vehicles were the only bright spot in Xiaomi's October sales report.
This is not unusual for a market that always cherishes the latest and greatest, with little regard for yesterday's champions. In the public's view, the SU7 and YU7 are already old cars, especially as competitor carmakers have been churning new models every month. There are only so many car buyers, and that race to get the newest toy has created unique challenges for carmakers in China.
Xiaomi has done well while it was the new kid on the block in 2024 and 2025, but this year, only the SkyNomad models have excited buyers. The shelf life of new car models in China is very short, forcing carmakers to make incredible efforts to bring new models without affecting profitability. This probably explains why carmakers have so many models that appear to overlap, or at least lack any distinctive features.
Xiaomi will likely miss the 2026 sales target, but what can it do? The SkyNomad brand might look successful now, but six months down the road, it might share Xiaomi SU7 and YU7's fate as the novelty wears out. Absent new model launches, Xiaomi might find itself slipping to the bottom of the Chinese sales charts. As fewer cars are bought, profitability suffers, and at some point, it will be forced to make a decision.
Photo: Xiaomi Auto Xiaomi has guided for 550,000 vehicles sold in 2026, and it appears to be on track to miss this target. During the January-October period, the company sold a total of 336,658 vehicles, which represents about 61% of its annual target. Reaching the 550,000-unit mark would require selling an average of over 106,000 vehicles in each of the final two months. That's more than double the October volume. Even with the year-end sales surge in China, that is a difficult task.
Since this is not the first time a Chinese carmaker (or, indeed, any carmaker operating in China) has hit a snag with local sales, it's highly likely that Xiaomi is already planning its next moves. The most obvious, which was announced a while back, is expanding to new markets. Xiaomi plans to start selling its EVs in Europe. Sales are expected to debut in early 2027 with the SU7 sedan.
This should provide a respite and offer Xiaomi some room to breathe, while also improving the profitability of its production lines. With healthy sales propped up by an anticipated European success, Xiaomi can continue investing in new vehicle lines at home, keeping the wheel spinning. This is the second move, expanding the vehicle lineup so that buyers stay hooked on the company's offers.

Photo: © Stevanovicigor | Dreamstime.com
By Alexander Whiteman
12 November 2026
Spain’s container terminals are beginning the task of recovering following yesterday’s general strike across the country that left box ships waiting at anchor after a slew of terminal closures – but the extent of the cargo backlog remains unclear.
Container movements ground to a halt at Algeciras, loading and discharge was suspended at Valencia, and cargo operations requiring the support of dockers stopped at Barcelona, although essential marine services remained unaffected.
Trade union confederation CCOO’s maritime-sector representative in Valencia for vessel operations, Francisco Martínez, told reporters: “There are no workers available, and there are no vessel operations.”
And while one forwarder told The Loadstar the strikes had “zero” impact on their operations, AIS tracking data showed the 1,072 teu Contship Zen still at anchor off Valencia last night, with an expectation of berthing this morning.
Similarly, the 20,124 teu Ever Gifted also appears to have remained at anchor off of the port, although it having arrived before the strike, its reason for being there may not be attributable to the labour action, even if it hinders efforts to clear the backlog.
The scale and duration of any backlog will depend on how quickly terminals restore normal productivity, and whether carriers have had to revise their rotations or roll cargo, but requests by The Loadstar to glean this information from terminal operators today have fallen on deaf ears.
Spain’s logistics employers’ association, UNO, suggested the wider impact on the country’s, and the EU’s, logistics and transport sector would be “limited and localised”, but did note that both Algeciras and Valencia would be exposed to the worst of the disruption.
Operations at both APMT’s Algeciras and Total Terminal International Algeciras were halted between 2am on 11 November and 2am on 12 November, bringing container movements to a standstill at one of the major Mediterranean transhipment hubs.
Another vessel seemingly awaiting a berth at Algeciras is the CMA CGM Tiga , AIS data showing it as having made slow approaches to the port after anchoring off it in the early hours of yesterday.
A spokesperson for APMT’s Spanish operations, which include Algeciras, told The Loadstar : “Minimum service levels established by the Spanish Ministry and Port Authorities for the 11 November general strike were fully met across APM Terminals’ facilities in Spain.
“In Algeciras, there was no participation in the strike by APMT employees or contractors, and the limited operational impact was primarily linked to previously announced weather-related restrictions in Campo de Gibraltar.”
To minimise disruption, the spokesperson noted that vessel operations were scheduled around the strike, while some terminals maintained services or extended operating hours to accommodate cargo flows, and added that all terminals were “currently operating normally”.
Despite UNO and the forwarder downplaying the strike’s impact, Juan Diego Pedrero, president of the Spanish Association of Private Railway Companies, told local media: “I don’t have percentages, but it is undoubtedly having an impact.”
Mr Pedrero added that “activity across the ports has heavily slowed, and this is affecting rail-port traffic, particularly at the ports of Valencia and Barcelona”, as local reports suggested dozens of freight services being cancelled.
